title: Meet Japan's 90-Year-Old Bodybuilding Champion
paragraphs: Many people slow down when they get older. But Toshisuke Kanazawa, a 90-year-old man from Japan, is still competing in bodybuilding competitions.
In August 2026, Kanazawa won the 85-and-over category at the Japan Masters Bodybuilding Championship in Hiroshima. According to reports, it was one of many national titles he has won.

Then, on October 30, 2026, Kanazawa took part in the IFBB World Fitness Championships in Santa Susanna, Spain. He competed in the masters category, which is for athletes aged 50 and older. This meant that many of the other competitors were decades younger than him. Before going on stage, Kanazawa warmed up with his team, and he put on a spray tan backstage, as bodybuilders often do to make their muscles easier to see. Kanazawa did not win a place on the podium, but he received a medal for taking part and proudly posed with it after the event.

Kanazawa has been building his muscles since he turned 50. He says he follows a strict diet. Since the age of 50, he has eaten only traditional Japanese food, such as brown rice, natto, which is made from fermented soybeans, and miso soup. He calls this "the classic Japanese way of eating." He also says he has not gotten sick in 90 years, and he believes this is because of his diet.

Kanazawa says he likes to try doing things that nobody else has done. He also talked about getting older. He said that people get more wrinkles as they age, and that in Japan, many people believe wrinkles make a person look less attractive. He also hopes to inspire older people to stay active and to show that age does not have to stop them.
Kanazawa says he wants to do bodybuilding for the rest of his life. He is even thinking about competing one more time when he is 93. After that, he says, he will probably retire.
